name: Zechariah
overview: Zechariah was a male member of the tribe of Judah, uniquely identified as the son of the Shilonite, according to Nehemiah 11:5. This designation highlights his lineage within a specific family group in Judah. No additional notes provide further details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Zechariah means "YHWH remembers," reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:5, was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotations consistent with biblical naming practices.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Zechariah was the son of Joiarib, an inference drawn from Nehemiah 11:5, and he is explicitly noted as an ancestor of Ahijah. Beyond these, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zechariah's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Judah as the son of the Shilonite and ancestor of Ahijah, situating him within the post-exilic community described in Nehemiah. His mention in Nehemiah 11:5 connects him to the restoration period when the people of Judah were resettling Jerusalem, underscoring the continuity of God's covenant people through faithful lineage.
